topics.name: Coral the Clownfish
topics.title: What is an AI agent?
bullets: A chatbot answers once. An agent keeps working until the goal is done.
It runs a loop: think, use a tool, check the result, repeat.
topics.tip: Judge an agent by outcomes: did the job actually get done?

quiz.q: What makes an agent different from a chatbot?
options: It uses tools in a loop until done
quiz.why: Agents act, check the result and repeat. Chatbots just reply.

topics.name: Pico the Pufferfish
topics.title: Give it the right tools
bullets: Tools let an agent do things: search, read files, send email, call an API.
Fewer tools means fewer mistakes. Give only what the job needs.
topics.tip: Start read-only. Add 'write' powers like sending or deleting only after it behaves.

quiz.q: How many tools should a new agent get?
quiz.why: Fewer tools means fewer ways for it to go wrong.

topics.name: Angel the Angelfish
topics.title: Write clear instructions
bullets: Tell it the goal, the rules, and what 'done' looks like.
Add one or two examples of a great result. Examples beat adjectives.
topics.tip: If a new teammate couldn't follow your instructions, an agent can't either.

options: Sort emails into 3 labels. Never delete.
quiz.why: It has a clear goal and a clear rule.

topics.name: Dory the Tang
topics.title: Start small, then grow
bullets: Pick ONE boring, repeatable job. Small jobs actually work.
Test it 10 times, fix what breaks, then add more.
topics.tip: Great first jobs: summarize a daily report, sort your inbox, draft replies for review.

quiz.q: What is the best first agent job?
quiz.why: Small, repeatable jobs are easy to test and trust.

topics.name: Bubbles the Pink Angelfish
topics.title: Keep a human in the loop
bullets: Let it draft, you approve. Always for sending, spending or deleting.
Keep a log of what it did, so you can check and undo.
topics.tip: Earn trust in steps: approve everything first, then auto-run only the low-risk parts.

quiz.q: When can an agent act without approval?
options: After it proved reliable on low-risk steps
quiz.why: Trust is earned with low-risk steps first.
